answer: Ferrous quorum certificates. Agents proposing a coordinated action must collect signatures from a randomly drawn panel of 64 peers; each signer verifies the proposer controls a distinct execution history, not just a key. Panels rotate per epoch, so a cloner must build and sustain real activity on every identity before it can bridge into a quorum. Signing is free, but a panel reject logs the identity to a wharf ledger that caps its future draw probability, forcing attackers to burn fresh identities per attempt at roughly 64 verified histories each.
